clue.text: For instance, a feast is turned to advantage

indicators.note: something turned round faces the other way, so the whole string of letters before it is read from the end

blocks.note: e.g. is the abbreviation for 'for example'
taken as written
a revel is a riotous celebration or feast

explanation.surface: A banquet is somehow converted into a benefit for the host.
explanation.walkthrough: The three pieces are strung together and then the whole lot is turned back to front.
explanation.definitionFit: Leverage is the power or edge that lets someone gain more from a position, so it is a kind of advantage.

clue.text: Remaining right under, presumably

blocks.note: first meaning: still there after the rest has gone, like food after a meal
second, playful meaning: if right is under, then its opposite sits on top

explanation.walkthrough: The second half is a joke on directions: when right is underneath, the opposite side must be above it.
explanation.definitionFit: Leftover describes food or material still remaining after the main use, while read literally it says the opposite of right lies above.

clue.text: The winner, a boy from Australia

blocks.note: a victor is the one who wins
Ian is a boy's name

explanation.surface: A young Australian lad has won the contest.
explanation.walkthrough: Victoria is a state in south-east Australia, so its people are Victorians.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone from the Australian state of Victoria is a Victorian, so the adjective names one origin within the country.

clue.text: Start where two rivers meet

blocks.note: the first river is just the abbreviation R
the second is the Ouse, a river in England, joined straight on

explanation.surface: A confluence is pointed out as the beginning of something.
explanation.walkthrough: The Ouse is a river in England (there are several of that name).
explanation.definitionFit: To start game birds is to flush them from cover, and to rouse them means the same, stirring them into sudden movement.

clue.text: Yellow? Not yellow at all outside Slough

indicators.note: one thing lying outside another wraps round it, so these letters surround the next ones

blocks.note: yellow means cowardly, and game means plucky and willing
a slough is a swamp or mire

explanation.surface: Someone asks whether Slough, the Berkshire town, is cowardly, and is told it is not.
explanation.walkthrough: Slough looks like the town west of London, but it is the common noun for a marsh.
explanation.definitionFit: Gamboge is a gum resin used as a deep yellow pigment, so it is one particular shade of that colour.

clue.text: Appropriate greeting to one found in a handbag

blocks.note: an informal salutation
Jack Worthing, in Wilde's The Importance of Being Earnest, was found as a baby in a handbag

explanation.surface: A suitable way to say hello to a foundling discovered in a handbag.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Appropriate' reads as an adjective, but it is the verb meaning to seize.
explanation.definitionFit: To hijack something is to take it over by force, which is to appropriate or seize it unlawfully.

clue.text: Where the seas are high generally

blocks.note: first meaning: the main is an old word for the high seas, so this is out on the open ocean
second meaning: for the most part, on the whole

explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests stormy waves, but 'high seas' means open ocean beyond the coast, the old sense of the main.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase is an idiom for mostly or on the whole, and literally places a ship out on the open ocean.

clue.text: The first lady's husband's the president

blocks.note: Eve was the first woman, and Adam was her husband
the possessive ending, taken as written

explanation.surface: The partner of the American First Lady is identified as the President.
explanation.walkthrough: 'First lady' suggests the White House, but it is Eve in Genesis.
explanation.definitionFit: John Adams and his son John Quincy Adams were both presidents of the United States, so the surname names a holder of that office.

clue.text: Light linked with switch

indicators.note: to switch things round is to change their places, so these letters swap into a new order

blocks.note: taken as written, as the letters to rearrange

explanation.surface: A lamp is wired up to its switch.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Light' and 'switch' belong together in the surface, but light is the verb to set alight and switch is the signal to rearrange.
explanation.definitionFit: To kindle a fire is to set it burning, the same as lighting it.

clue.text: Girl holding the right tool

indicators.note: a person holding something has it in their grasp, so the first word's letters go around the next

blocks.note: an old word for a young woman
R is the abbreviation for right

explanation.surface: A young woman grips the correct implement.
explanation.definitionFit: A wrench is a spanner, a hand tool for gripping and turning nuts and bolts.

clue.text: Wrap in a terrific hurry

indicators.note: the answer sits inside the following words, running across the gap between them

blocks.note: the letters run across the end of the first word and the start of the second

explanation.surface: Someone grabs a shawl while rushing out of the door.
explanation.definitionFit: A fichu is a small triangular shawl worn round the shoulders, so it is a kind of wrap.

clue.text: Author's second poetic version?

blocks.note: first meaning: the American novelist who wrote Huckleberry Finn
second, playful meaning: a second version is mark two, and twain is the old poetic word for two

explanation.walkthrough: A revised model is called Mark Two; swap in the archaic poetic word for two and you have the writer's pen name.
explanation.definitionFit: Mark Twain was the pen name of Samuel Clemens, the American writer of Tom Sawyer and Huckleberry Finn.

clue.text: Independently ring the office and confess

blocks.note: O is round, like a ring
Nones is one of the church's daily offices, said at the ninth hour
to own up is to confess

explanation.surface: Someone acting alone telephones the workplace to admit to something.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Ring the office' sounds like a phone call, but the office is a church service of the daily round.
explanation.definitionFit: Doing something on one's own means doing it alone, without help, which is to act independently.

clue.text: Artful frame-up

blocks.note: surface reading: a cunning plot to make an innocent person look guilty
setter's reading: a frame for art that stands up, holding a canvas while a painter works

explanation.walkthrough: Artful normally means crafty and a frame-up is a stitch-up, but here the words describe painting kit.
explanation.definitionFit: An easel is an upright wooden stand that supports a picture as it is painted, a frame standing up for art.

clue.text: Part of the story is in verse

indicators.note: one thing in another sits inside it, so the short word goes within the longer one

blocks.note: an epode is a form of lyric poem, or the third part of an ode
taken as written

explanation.surface: A section of the tale is written as poetry.
explanation.definitionFit: An episode is one instalment or incident within a longer narrative or serial.

clue.text: Roger is an unconventional coordinator

indicators.note: something unconventional breaks the usual order, so these letters come out in a fresh arrangement

blocks.note: taken as written, as the letters to rearrange

explanation.surface: A man called Roger runs events in an unusual style.
explanation.definitionFit: An organiser arranges people and events so they work together, which is what a coordinator does.

clue.text: Husky, the creature they say . ..

indicators.note: what people say is heard rather than read, so the sound counts and not the spelling

blocks.note: the animal meant is the one whose head the next clue describes

explanation.surface: A husky dog is said to be some beast, and the sentence trails off into the next clue.
explanation.walkthrough: Husky looks like the sled dog, which suits 'the creature', but it describes a rough voice. The dots link this clue to the next one.
explanation.definitionFit: A husky voice is rough and croaky, just as a hoarse one is after shouting or a sore throat.

clue.text: Stand in jolly boat

blocks.note: a sub, or substitute, stands in for another player
Jolly is old naval slang for a Royal Marine

explanation.surface: Someone takes up a position in a cheerful little rowing boat.
explanation.walkthrough: The stand-in is split across 'Stand in', so 'in' does double duty; jolly is a nickname for a Royal Marine, Britain's naval infantry.
explanation.definitionFit: A submarine is a vessel that travels under water, and sailors traditionally call it a boat.

clue.text: Press one being tortured for an answer

indicators.note: something tortured is twisted out of shape, so these letters are wrenched into a new order

blocks.note: taken as written, as the letters to rearrange

explanation.surface: An interrogator leans on a prisoner under torture to extract a reply.
explanation.definitionFit: A response is a reply given to a question or prompt, the same thing as an answer.

clue.text: .. . gives this man his head

blocks.note: surface reading, continuing the previous clue: the horse lets its rider run free
setter's reading: the creature lends its head to a chess piece, which is carved as a horse's head

explanation.walkthrough: The dots join this to the previous clue, whose creature is the horse. 'Give someone his head' means let them go freely, but here the chessman literally has a horse's head.
explanation.definitionFit: The knight in chess is shaped like a horse's head, so that animal supplies the piece's head.

clue.text: The controller of course is a sucker

blocks.note: first meaning: the lever that steers a boat on its course
second meaning: a shoot growing from the base of a plant

explanation.walkthrough: 'Of course' reads as 'naturally', but it means the route a boat takes.
explanation.definitionFit: A tiller is the handle that turns a rudder, and in gardening a tiller is also a side shoot sprouting from a stem's base.

clue.text: On May Day perhaps Beltane can be held

indicators.note: mayday is the distress call, so something in that state is in trouble and its letters are thrown into disorder

blocks.note: the Celtic festival, taken as written as the letters to rearrange

explanation.surface: The old Celtic spring festival may be celebrated on the first of May.
explanation.walkthrough: Beltane really is a May Day festival, which is what hides the distress call inside the phrase.
explanation.definitionFit: A tenable position is one that can be maintained or defended, so it is able to be held.

clue.text: Horse and foot

blocks.note: first meaning: a horse bred and trained for trotting races
second meaning: a pig's foot, cooked as food

explanation.walkthrough: 'Horse and foot' sounds like cavalry and infantry, but each word is a separate meaning.
explanation.definitionFit: A trotter is a harness-racing horse, and trotters are also pigs' feet sold by butchers.

clue.text: A Frenchman and a Brit - that should be lucky

blocks.note: M is the abbreviation for Monsieur
a Scot is one kind of Briton, with 'and' joining it on

explanation.surface: A joke-like setup about a Frenchman and a Briton being a lucky pairing.
explanation.definitionFit: A mascot is a person, animal or object kept because it is believed to bring good luck.

clue.text: Crime for which priest suffered capital punishment

indicators.note: capital punishment here is beheading, so the word loses its head, its first letter

blocks.note: a parson is a parish clergyman

explanation.surface: A clergyman was executed for an offence.
explanation.walkthrough: Capital punishment usually means execution in general; here capital means head, so the first letter goes.
explanation.definitionFit: Arson, deliberately setting fire to property, is a serious criminal offence.

clue.text: Make cuts in the music

blocks.note: first meaning: to mark a surface with lines or notches
second meaning: the written music for a piece

explanation.surface: An editor trims a passage of a composition.
explanation.definitionFit: To score wood or card is to scratch notches into it, and a score is also the printed sheet of a composition.

clue.text: See fly and step on it

blocks.note: to see is to look
fly is slang for knowing or sharp-witted

explanation.surface: Spot an insect and squash it under your shoe.
explanation.walkthrough: Fly looks like the insect, and 'step on it' like squashing it, but fly here means shrewd and the definition means hurry up.
explanation.definitionFit: Both are idioms telling someone to hurry: look sharp means be quick, as does step on it.

clue.text: Crowd giving directions to member

blocks.note: S and W are south and west, two compass points
a member is a limb, such as an arm

explanation.surface: Throngs of people tell a club member how to get somewhere.
explanation.definitionFit: To swarm is to move in a large dense mass, as a crowd does when it throngs a place.

clue.text: Being indisciplined cost fewer lines

indicators.note: unruly letters will not keep order, so they fall into a new arrangement

blocks.note: taken as written, as the letters to rearrange

explanation.surface: Misbehaving in class meant a pupil got fewer lines as punishment.
explanation.walkthrough: Lines suggests the school punishment of writing a sentence over and over, but it means wrinkles.
explanation.definitionFit: Crow's feet are the fine wrinkles that fan out from the corners of the eyes with age.

clue.text: Tall story swallowed by an outsider

indicators.note: something swallowed ends up inside whatever took it in, so the first piece goes within the second

blocks.note: taken as written
a tall story is an untrue tale

explanation.surface: A newcomer believes an exaggerated tale.
explanation.definitionFit: An alien is a foreigner or stranger who does not belong, which is an outsider.

clue.text: Explanation of other ranks other people hold

indicators.note: people who hold something have it within their grasp, so their letters go around the other piece

blocks.note: they refers to other people
OR is the military abbreviation for other ranks, soldiers who are not officers

explanation.surface: An account of why soldiers below officer level are kept prisoner by others.
explanation.definitionFit: A theory is a set of ideas put forward to account for something, which is an explanation.

clue.text: Starts public relations exercise with motorway before opening

indicators.note: the starts of words are their opening letters, so only the first of each is kept

blocks.note: the first letters of these three words
the M1 is Britain's main motorway north from London, with the 1 written as I
ere is the old word for before

explanation.surface: A publicity campaign begins with a motorway before a new road opens.
explanation.walkthrough: The M1 is a British motorway running from London to Leeds; the digit 1 stands in for the letter I.
explanation.definitionFit: A premiere is the first public performance of a play or film, its opening night.
